title: Treat a blank docker-compose ${VAR:-} env var as absent (not as the empty-string value)

invented_rule.summary: docker-compose ${VAR:-} emits Ok("") (empty string) to the container — not Err(NotPresent) — so callers must explicitly filter empty strings to treat blank the same as absent; a reader that treats Ok("") as a valid value silently uses an empty string as the configured value.
invented_rule.absent_from_pretraining_rationale: The docker-compose ${VAR:-} blank-equals-absent rule is a discovered interaction between docker-compose's env passthrough syntax and Rust's std::env::var — it is not covered in standard Rust or docker-compose documentation. A generic solver would likely check only Err(NotPresent) and not Ok(""), since the normal mental model for 'optional environment variable' is that absence means the variable is not set at all.

prompt:
In `src/config.rs`, the `embed_model` function reads the optional `OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL` environment variable to determine which embedding model to use, defaulting to `"qwen3-embedding:4b"` if not set.

The docker-compose file uses `${OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL:-}` for optional passthrough, which emits `Ok("")` (empty string) when the host variable is unset — NOT `Err(NotPresent)`.

The current implementation only handles `Err(NotPresent)`:

```rust
pub fn embed_model() -> String {
    std::env::var("OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL")
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| "qwen3-embedding:4b".to_string())
}
```

This silently uses an empty string as the model name when the variable is set-but-blank. Fix `embed_model` so that both missing AND blank values fall back to the default `"qwen3-embedding:4b"`.
